lead: Villas with gardens, tree-lined avenues and one of the highest incomes in Barcelona.
text: It was part of the former municipality of Sarrià and is one of the neighbourhoods where much of the Catalan industrial bourgeoisie has lived, with houses with gardens and stately buildings. It began as a neighbourhood between 1901 and 1903, when some residents who had come from Sants built three villas, one for each of them, and its oldest part is around the market, between Carrer de Vergós and Carrer d'Escoles Pies.

It is a small (0.79 km²) and quiet neighbourhood, with the Diagonal and its shopping centres, such as L'Illa and El Corte Inglés, a short step away. At 2,014 €/month, it has the highest average rent in Barcelona, and its sale price, 5,743 €/m², is below that of Sarrià and Sant Gervasi-Galvany. If you are selling, the average sale price is practically in line with the Sarrià-Sant Gervasi average. Within the neighbourhood, the price of each flat depends on its condition, its floor and its building, so it is best to compare it with nearby sales rather than with the district average. If you are buying, an 80 m² flat costs about 459,000 € on average, and this neighbourhood sits in the middle band of Sarrià-Sant Gervasi (3rd of 6 by price). If you are investing, the average rent is 26% above the district; before deciding, it is worth studying each deal with real figures for purchase, renovation and rental income.
housing: Houses with gardens and low-rise stately buildings, with spacious flats.
